```sh
kafka config unset <names...>
```

Remove one or more config entries from a resource, reverting them to default

## Arguments

| Argument   | Description              |
| ---------- | ------------------------ |
| `names...` | resource names to update |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Removes the named overrides so broker defaults apply; use --dry-run for validation.

## Before you run

Removes explicit settings and exposes inherited/default values. Record the old overrides before removal so they can be restored.

## Flags

| Flag                          | Description                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`          | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092                      |
| `--type <string>`             | resource type: topic, broker, broker-logger, client-metrics, or group |
| `--key <string> (repeatable)` | a config key to remove (repeatable)                                   |
| `--dry-run`                   | validate without changing anything                                    |

## Examples

```sh
kafka config unset --type topic orders --key retention.ms
kafka config unset --type topic orders payments --key cleanup.policy --dry-run
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": []
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
